articles.title: One Word for Every Top 25 Men's CBB Team's Start to the 2026-27 Season
articles.summary: Though it feels like the 2026-27 men's college basketball season just started yesterday, most teams have already played more than 15 percent of their regular-season schedule.
articles.body:
Though it feels like the 2026-27 men's college basketball season just started yesterday, most teams have already played more than 15 percent of their regular-season schedule.

How are the alleged best teams in the nation looking through these first few weeks?

Using Monday's AP Top 25, we've put together a one-word synopsis for each team in the poll.

Some of those teams have exceeded expectations to an astounding degree.

Others...not so much. (And that doesn't even include Kentucky, who fell out of the rankings before we could comment on that whole situation.)

Unless otherwise noted, statistics are current through the start of play on Wednesday.

Nos. 25-22: LSU, Nebraska, Louisville and Gonzaga

Will Wade's roster at LSU was the ultimate experiment in building a team within the SEC and NCAA framework. So far, though, the experiment has been a success: LSU routed three overmatched opponents before going on the road for a come-from-behind victory over Gonzaga. For a guy who had retired from playing basketball earlier this year, Donovan Dent sure looks like an All-American. (Now that RJ Luis Jr. is playing, though, let's see what happens to/with LSU.)

Nebraska was more than a little sloppy in the 67-58 win over Providence, shooting 21 percent from distance and committing 13 dead-ball turnovers—shot clock violations, five-second violations, throwing the ball out of bounds, etc. But the Cornhuskers entered Wednesday night's game against South Dakota shooting 70.5 percent inside the arc while also averaging 10.5 threes per game. They were proficient on offense last year, but early returns suggest they are going to be even more unstoppable this season.

We know that Louisville is going to fire up a ton of three-point shots. Pat Kelsey's teams always do. However, the Cardinals shot 25.7 percent (9-for-35) in their opener against Chattanooga. And after draining six of their first nine attempts whilst opening up a 38-23 lead over Memphis, the Cardinals missed each and every one of their final 17 attempts en route to a 20-point loss. Can Seth Trimble, Karter Knox and Adrian Wooley turn things around? Or is their combined 6-for-36 start to the season a sign of impending doom?

Gonzaga led by 13 with eight minutes remaining against LSU. It blew that game. The Zags also led by 11 with less than six minutes to go in the opener against Purdue, only to watch the Boilermakers storm back and almost take the lead. Gonzaga wasn't particularly dominant in its home win over Montana State, either. While we're nowhere close to panicking about the dancing streak that dates back to 1999, they certainly haven't been "Peak Zags" thus far.

BYU entered play on Wednesday ranked fifth in the nation in three-point percentage and 10th in two-point percentage, averaging 96.5 points per game. That includes dropping 94 on Ohio State on opening night. Rob Wright III is the star of the show, but he is surrounded by guys who can pour in buckets. Though the defense is a far cry from championship level and figures to ultimately be their undoing in March, BYU's offense is giving off 2018 Villanova vibes.

Of the 11 Razorbacks who have appeared in at least two of the team's first five games, eight are freshmen. And while John Calipari is no stranger to relying heavily upon first-year players, an experience disparity was on full display in the loss to Indiana and especially in the loss to Virginia, which got out of hand in a hurry. Jordan Smith Jr. and Co. clearly have a lot of talent, but how long will it take this team to jell on defense and unlock its potential?

USC always seems to have one of the tallest rosters in the country, but this year, the Trojans have 6'10" Jacob Cofie, 6'11" Adonis Ratliff and 7'0" Darius Ratliff all in their starting lineup. And that trio has already racked up 22 blocks for a team that has owned the paint. Granted, USC has yet to face a true contender. We'll see how things go against Texas Tech in mid-December, as well as against the likes of Illinois and Michigan State in Big Ten play. But they're looking large and in charge so far.

*USC and Michigan are tied at No. 18. However, the Trojans were left off seven ballots while the Wolverines appeared in all but one, so we're putting USC where No. 19 ought to be.

Nos. 18-16: Michigan, Miami (FL) and Alabama

Connecticut did a fantastic job of keeping Michigan from getting out and running the floor, and won convincingly as a result. In the Wolverines' other three games, however, they have outscored their competition by a 62-4 margin on fast-break points. And aside from those first 25 minutes against the Huskies, they've looked a bit better than expected.

Since putting up a respectable fight in a 77-67 opening night loss to Florida, the Hurricanes have held Wagner, North Florida, North Alabama and Rider to 52.0 points per game. To put it lightly, those aren't Final Four contenders, so take it with a grain of salt. But Miami has already held more opponents to 39.0 percent or worse on two-point attempts (four times) than it did in the entire 2025-26 campaign (three times). Could be a dangerous team in next week's Players Era 16 tournament.

Nate Oats' teams only know one speed, consistently playing at one of the fastest tempos in the country while also taking seemingly as many three-point attempts as possible. So, it's hardly a surprise that the Crimson Tide are averaging 99.4 points and 34.4 three-point attempts per game. And now that they're good and warmed up, it's time to find out how this year's bunch fares against real competition. They'll draw Baylor and potentially Gonzaga and Michigan in the Players Era 16 before continuing nonconference play against Miami (FL), Houston and St. John's.

New 2027 Men's NCAA Tournament Bracket Projections 🔮

Nos. 15-13: Vanderbilt, Tennessee and St. John's

KenPom certainly smells what the Commodores are cooking, presently rating them as the fifth-best team in the country. Vanderbilt has won each of its first five games by at least 23 points, including a 105-81 shellacking of a Memphis team that has already beaten Louisville, Iowa State and VCU. Rebounding was not a strength for Vandy last year, but the 'Dores have been dominant on the glass thus far, finishing at least +11 in rebounding margin in each game. And Washington State transfer Ace Glass has been quite the complement to Tyler Tanner in this backcourt.

Tennessee uncharacteristically struggled with Tennessee State last Friday, allowing 78 points in a close call against the type of foe that it typically destroys by something like an 89-60 margin. What a motivating factor that turned out to be for Rick Barnes, though, as the Volunteers came out in their next game and absolutely smothered Michigan State for a 61-46 upset. The Spartans made 24 free throws but shot just 9-for-50 from the field. (The starting five went 3-for-28.) Could this be Barnes' best defense yet?

Through four comfortable victories, St. John's has averaged 19.3 turnovers forced while allowing 7.8 offensive rebounds and 12.0 free-throw attempts. And in the one game that reasonably could have been competitive, the Red Storm turned over Syracuse 21 times and allowed just five second-chance points. But what else is new with Rick Pitino? His best teams have always been elite on defense.

Nos. 12-10: Arizona, Kansas and Illinois

In Ivan Kharchenkov, Mo Krivas, Caleb Holt and Derek Dixon, Arizona probably has the best quartet in the nation. At any rate, they're combining for north of 70 points per game. But as the Wildcats continue their fight to get RJ Godfrey eligible to play, depth is already a considerable concern for this team, especially in the frontcourt. Freshman Cameron Holmes might be the best candidate to eventually fill that void, but he has yet to make any sort of impact against a respectable foe.

Melvin Council Jr. played in two games before suffering a broken foot. He'll likely be out for two months. And then in Kansas' second game without Council, superstar freshman Tyran Stokes suffered a bone bruise in his right knee and missed Wednesday's game against West Virginia. At least he should be back in short order, but the Jayhawks are a very far cry from full strength at the moment. (And still somehow beat a pretty good WVU squad to set up a colossal game against Houston on Thursday.)

If you've only watched 10 percent of Illinois' season thus far, here's hoping it wasn't the first half at Texas Tech when they were outscored 49-29. Because aside from that, the Illini have been a tour de force, punctuated by the 99-78 road win over Duke this week. What is patently absurd about this team averaging north of 103 points per game is they've done it without their best player, David Mirkovic, and they've done it despite losing Jake Davis—who had a nation-best 146.6 O-rating last season—to a shoulder injury in the first half of their season opener. Just imagine if they get healthy.

Among Texas Tech's seven leaders in minutes played, the Red Raiders have four fifth-year seniors, one conventional senior and a pair of juniors. They do have one freshman big man (Bassala Bagayoko) in their starting five, but goodness knows he'll be relegated to a reserve role if senior JT Toppin is able to return from the torn ACL suffered in February. And that stockpile of experience was huge in the win over Illinois, both pacing the Red Raiders to a 22-point lead and having the composure to not completely collapse when the Illini made their comeback push.

In its decade-plus under Kelvin Sampson, Houston has consistently been excellent on defense and one of the strongest/toughest teams of all. But this Cougars team, in particular, promises to be special in the paint. Through the first two games of the Players Era 8, they shot a combined 8-for-22 from three-point range. Yet, they defeated both Rutgers and Florida by double digits by owning the glass and letting Dedan Thomas Jr. cook with his dribble-drive action. Houston presently has the lowest three-point rate in the country.

That would be Nikola Kusturica, UCLA's 17-year-old from Serbia who has taken college basketball by storm. He's averaging 17.3 points, 5.5 rebounds, 2.8 assists, 1.8 blocks and 1.5 steals while shooting 44 percent from beyond the arc. In the season-opening victory over Arizona, he didn't shoot it well, but he did "impact winning" on both ends of the floor. And since then, he has been the MVP of a freight train that smashed through North Florida, Arkansas Pine Bluff and Long Beach State.

Texas' pre-Thanksgiving schedule consists of five home games against bottom-100 competition and a neutral-site game against Baylor. They blew out the first three cream puffs and then narrowly survived a back-and-forth battle with the unranked Bears. The only thing we know for sure here is that big man Matas Vokietaitis is still a certified problem for opposing teams. And if he has actually figured out how to play without getting into foul trouble, look out.

Duke eviscerated Army, Coastal Carolina and SIU-Edwardsville by a combined margin of 138 points. But against real competition—Michigan State and Illinois—the Blue Devils got thrown around like rag dolls. Jeremy Fears and Jordan Scott clearly wanted the first game more than anyone on Duke's roster did. Same goes for Andrej Stojakovic and especially Quentin Coleman in the latter. Shooting below 25 percent from distance in each game certainly didn't help matters, but Duke needs to figure out how to play a lot tougher, especially on defense.

Preseason ACC Player of the Year Thijs De Ridder is the straw that stirs the drink here, but losing him to foul trouble almost immediately against Arkansas did nothing to slow the Cavaliers down. All five starters went for at least 13 points in that one, as the more experienced, well-rounded team cruised to victory. De Ridder has gone for at least 15 points and six rebounds in each game of UVA's 6-0 start, but Sam Lewis, Chance Mallory and Johann Grunloh are just as likely to take over any given game.

Nos. 3-1: Connecticut, Michigan State and Florida

The Huskies have already beaten Michigan and Ohio State. They also lost at Arizona. They still have games remaining against Duke, Illinois, Kansas and Virginia in the next five weeks. By the time conference play arrives, no one will be more battle-tested than Dan Hurley's guys. They've already looked like a title contender, and it's sounding like they're going to get Solo Ball back sooner than expected.

To the surprise of nobody, Jeremy Fears Jr. is looking like the most important player in the country. He only had two assists in Tuesday's loss to Tennessee, despite not officially recording a field-goal attempt until early in the second half. Such is life when no one on the roster can make a shot that night. But he entered that game averaging 16.8 points and 10.0 assists per game, shredding Duke to the tune of 18 points, 11 assists and seven rebounds in the Champions Classic. Still waiting to see who becomes the Robin to this Batman, but Fears might lead the nation in both assists and made free throws this season.

The preseason favorite to win the national championship, Florida has yet to really showcase that expected dominance. Against each of Miami (FL), Florida State and Notre Dame, the Gators won by 8-10 points, but there was a point midway through the second half in which the underdog had the ball with a chance to either tie or take the lead. And then against Houston on Wednesday, Florida shot 58 percent from three-point range and still lost by 10. That isn't to say we're concerned about the Gators. Just...underwhelmed.

articles.title: Report Card Grades for Every NBA Team So Far
articles.summary: It's officially safe to start making assumptions about your favorite NBA players and teams, as the sample size has grown large enough now with nearly 20 percent of the 2026-27 regular season complete.
articles.body:
It's officially safe to start making assumptions about your favorite NBA players and teams, as the sample size has grown large enough now with nearly 20 percent of the 2026-27 regular season complete.

This means it's time to hand out report card grades for all 30 squads, with factors like record, net rating, injuries and preseason expectations all being considered.

Is your team acing its early-season exam? Or is some more tutoring clearly needed?

ATL | BKN | BOS | CHA | CHI | CLE | DAL | DEN | DET | GSW | HOU | IND | LAC | LAL | MEM | MIA | MIL | MIN | NOP | NYK | OKC | ORL | PHI | PHX | POR | SAC | SAS | TOR | UTA | WAS

The Atlanta Hawks are mostly what we thought they would be: a good (albeit not great) team in an improved East that will be fighting for one of the final guaranteed playoff spots.

This team needs Jalen Johnson to play like an All-Star once again, as his scoring has dipped to 19.5 points on a measly 18.2 percent shooting from three. As a result, the typically high-powered Hawks offense sits at just 18th overall this season.

Making the switch from veteran CJ McCollum to rookie Kingston Flemings in the starting lineup will come with some growing pains, as McCollum (calf, four weeks) now joins Asa Newell (toe surgery, four months) on the injury list.

This could be a sneaky trade destination for stars around the deadline as the Hawks look to jump into the upper echelon of Eastern Conference teams.

Considering such a franchise-altering offseason trade and how much talent has been stripped off this roster since the 2024 title, the Boston Celtics are one of the most impressive teams in the NBA right now.

Owners of the best net rating in the league and sniffing the top record in the East, the Celtics should be thrilled with how the season has begun.

Paul George has missed just two games all year and been a reliable No. 2 scorer (20.8 points, 44.3 percent from three) alongside Jayson Tatum, who's embraced his role as the primary playmaker (7.1 assists) in addition to his scoring duties.

This defense has been elite ( 106.1 rating, No. 2 in NBA ), helping to smooth over any transition woes from Jaylen Brown to George.

Are the Brooklyn Nets bad? Yes. Are they among the worst teams in the NBA? No, and, hey, that's progress.

Seven teams still rank behind Brooklyn in net rating , as the Nets have had a trio of close losses to some good teams in addition to their three victories.

Veteran forwards Julius Randle and Michael Porter Jr. are keeping Brooklyn competitive, but this team needs more development from its seven first-round picks over the past two drafts. Mikel Brown Jr., the No. 6 overall pick this past summer, still hasn't carved out a starting role.

The 11-4 Houston Rockets own swap rights with the Nets this season, meaning Brooklyn isn't even in line to cash in on a top pick, either.

It's been a rough season already, although we shouldn't have been expecting much more.

Biggest NBA Surprises and Disappointments 🏀

It's been a woeful start to the season for the Charlotte Hornets, a franchise that's trying to remake its image in the post-LaMelo Ball era.

Injuries have limited Coby White to just six games and Kon Knueppel to six minutes, resulting in an offense that ranks dead last in the NBA ( 103.1 rating ). Brandon Miller is struggling after signing a five-year, $208.3 million extension, as his 34.4 percent shooting mark overall ranks 145th out of 146 players who have attempted at least 100 shots this season.

Charlotte needs a healthy White and Knueppel to orchestrate any sort of a scoring attack, as the Hornets also rank last overall in assist ratio and turnover percentage.

The Chicago Bulls made a real effort to get better this past summer, adding veterans Norman Powell, Nic Claxton and Buddy Hield while drafting Caleb Wilson at No. 4 overall.

Unfortunately, these moves haven't led to many wins as of yet. The Bulls have the worst defense in the NBA (120.0 rating), Josh Giddey's scoring has dropped nearly in half (9.9 points per game) and Claxton has been injured for most of the season.

The good news is that Wilson (18.9 points, 6.2 rebounds, 1.8 steals) looks like a future star and the team's defense is already noticeably better in the short amount of time Claxton has spent on the floor ( minus-12.5 defensive swing rating ).

We're not asking Chicago to make the playoffs, although this team should at least be competing for a play-in spot given the mix of veteran and young talent.

The Cleveland Cavaliers have been one of the most unpredictable teams in the NBA all season.

From blowing a 29-point lead on opening night to the Philadelphia 76ers to going down by 33 to the lowly Charlotte Hornets (and ultimately losing), the Cavs have looked completely lost at times. They've also looked like a Finals contender, beating the 76ers and Knicks and defeating the Mavericks while resting all five starters.

James Harden appears to be out of shape and showing his age at 37, and the Cavs have a net rating of plus-10.9 when the veteran point guard is on the bench. In his 952 on-court possessions, Cleveland's net rating plunges to minus-1.6 .

For a team trying to win a title, there's actually a nice, young talent base being assembled here. Evan Mobley, Peyton Watson, Jaylon Tyson, Meleek Thomas and Tyrese Proctor are all 25 or younger, giving the Cavs some room for internal growth or some potential future trade assets.

A 7-4 record to begin the season for the Dallas Mavericks was a nice surprise, although three straight ugly losses (including to a Cleveland Cavaliers team resting all five starters) should be extremely concerning for Mavs fans.

Cooper Flagg and Kyrie Irving are absolutely carrying this team right now, as Dallas has a net rating of plus-6.8 with both stars on the floor vs. minus-24.4 when the pair needs to rest. That's a wild difference and speaks to the youth and collective talent of the rest of this roster.

The Mavs may have to sell high on Irving at some point, as this is a franchise short on future draft picks that needs to build up a bigger young talent base around Flagg. The overall record is fine, but the team's offense and defense both rank in the bottom half of the NBA.

A good offense, bad defense and questionable bench? The Denver Nuggets are back, baby!

This team doesn't look anywhere close to being a title contender right now, as only one of Denver's seven victories has come against a team with a winning record. Three of the seven are against the New Orleans Pelicans.

A 20th-ranked defense simply isn't going to cut it, and a (slight) dip in play from Nikola Jokić overall means the three-time MVP is beginning to show his age (32 in February).

For a team that's still about $3 million over the second apron , a trade is coming at some point to cut salary. It's hard to imagine that such a deal is actually going to get the Nuggets closer to winning a title this season, as this roster still needs a lot of help even with Jamal Murray enjoying a career year.

Despite a lack of offseason activity, the Detroit Pistons have held a top-3 seed in the East even with starting center Jalen Duren missing all but two games due to injury.

Detroit also has a trio of quality wins on its resume, beating the Boston Celtics, Philadelphia 76ers and San Antonio Spurs. The combined record of those three opponents is 35-9.

Cade Cunningham should be in the MVP conversation with his 25.7 points, 5.2 rebounds, 7.9 assists and 1.5 steals per game, as he's had to do everything for an offense that features few other scoring options and ranks just 15th overall .

Still, a top-5 defense has carried over from last year and a healthy Duren will make a big difference. The Pistons should be mostly pleased with their start to the season.

How good are the Golden State Warriors? That question still depends entirely on if Stephen Curry is in the game.

When he is on the court, the Warriors have been elite with a 7-2 record in his nine full games. Golden State has a net rating of plus-13.5 in Curry's floor time, yet it is 1-4 in games he's missed or gotten hurt in with a net rating of minus-8.3 .

Even at age 38, Curry is still one of the most valuable players in the NBA.

Curry is sidelined until around the middle of December with an oblique abdominal tear. His Warriors have gotten off to a strong start but are now in danger of fading.

It's surprisingly been an elite offense that's carried the Houston Rockets so far this season, thanks in part to the return of a healthy Fred VanVleet. The veteran point guard is shooting 47.6 percent from three over his last six games and has 65 total assists against just 12 turnovers in his first 12 games.

Houston has done a great job of winning the games they're supposed to, with just a single loss to a team with a losing record so far (the 6-7 Phoenix Suns). This is the second-best offensive rebounding team in the NBA despite Steven Adams playing in just two games thus far and is one of the most physical groups in the league.

Kevin Durant (21.3 points, 5.5 rebounds, 3.8 assists, 1.1 blocks) is still playing at a high level at age 38 and six total scorers are averaging double figures.

This is a title contender, especially if the defense continues to improve.

The Indiana Pacers are 2-2 in Tyrese Haliburton's healthy games this season, yet have slid to 3-7 since the All-Star guard suffered a hamstring injury. He looked really good in a return from a torn Achilles (21.8 points, 9.5 assists, 4.5 rebounds, 1.3 steals) and could be back by the end of this month.

A 22nd-ranked offense this season mostly without Haliburton (and T.J. McConnell) is perfectly understandable and should rise dramatically upon his return. Pascal Siakam is again looking like an All-Star, although fourth-year forward Jarace Walker (6.5 points, 27.7 percent from three) has taken a step back following a breakout season.

It's tough to grade the Pacers right now without their leader, although the team is still clinging on to a play-in spot in the East.

The new-look Los Angeles Clippers are sorely missing Brandon Ingram and Bradley Beal, as neither veteran has made his season debut due to injury.

Darius Garland (21.2 points, 6.9 assists) is doing everything he can to lead the offense, although having 38-year-old, part-time starter Brook Lopez as the team's second-leading scorer (14.8 points per game) tells you a lot about the state of the Clippers right now.

This roster is made up almost entirely of role players who are all being asked to do too much, especially with Ingram sidelined. Rival teams should treat the Clippers like a supermarket come trade deadline time, as there are plenty of rotation guys who could help out a contender to shop for here.

The Oklahoma City Thunder own first-round pick swap rights with Los Angeles, so even a bad season likely won't result in a top draft selection. The Clippers have to hope that Ingram and Beal can return to the floor, rookie Keaton Wagler develops quickly and Garland continues to play at a high level to return to the play-in part of the West.

The Los Angeles Lakers own both the best record in the NBA and the league's top offense (121.6 rating), thanks mostly to Luka Dončić's incredible season.

A 38.8-point-per-game scoring average doesn't even look real, as Dončić is nearly a full eight points higher than Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, the league's second-leading scorer.

One can't argue with the record, although there are some concerns here. Los Angeles ranks just 17th defensively and 16th in rebounding while Dončić's usage rate of 40.4 percent is currently the third-highest in NBA history .

As much as he'd likely love to keep having the ball in his hands this much, having Dončić fresh for a playoff run is more important.

The Memphis Grizzlies are the biggest and best surprise of the 2026-27 NBA season, no questions asked.

While most of us assumed this would be a rebuilding year for the young Grizzlies, Memphis owns the third-best offense and fourth-highest net rating in the entire NBA. Ty Jerome has been a monster this season in a leading role, as his 25.4 points per game rank 12th in the league.

This kind of record has been a team effort, however, as a whopping eight players are averaging at least 10 points. Cameron Boozer, the No. 3 overall pick, ranks 12th in the NBA in rebounding (9.5) and is tied for the Grizzlies team lead in assists (5.4).

If Jerome can shake off previous injury woes, this could be a top-four seed in the West.

It was a rough start for the Miami Heat, who began the season 0-4 but are now riding a five-game winning streak.

Giannis Antetokounmpo (28.3 points, 12.5 rebounds, 5.2 assists) has been consistently great, yet it's been the play of the starting backcourt that's made the biggest difference in Miami's turnaround.

Klay Thompson is averaging 19.3 points, 3.0 assists and making 47.6 percent of his three-pointers during the win streak, including a whopping 5.0 threes per game. Davion Mitchell now leads the NBA in assists (9.2) and is giving the Heat 17.8 points, 4.0 rebounds, 11.0 assists and 1.6 steals over his last five games.

For a team that entered the season with real concerns about guard play and shooting around Antetokounmpo, Miami has gotten some stellar play as of late.

The Milwaukee Bucks and Sacramento Kings are currently in a battle for the worst team in the NBA. The big difference? The Kings still have the rights to their 2027 first-round pick.

At least the Brewers won the World Series?

There's nothing going right with the Bucks right now. Milwaukee has the worst record in the NBA, the worst net rating in the NBA and the team is still mostly rolling with a veteran-heavy starting lineup.

Myles Turner, despite standing nearly seven feet tall, is shooting just 36.0 percent overall from the field. That's the seventh-worst mark in NBA history among players 6'11" or taller.

This team should look very different after the trade deadline, as players like Kel'el Ware, Brayden Burries, Nate Ament, Ryan Rollins and others get their playing time prioritized.

Few teams could lose a talent like Anthony Edwards and continue to play at a high level. Major credit goes to this Minnesota Timberwolves coaching staff and players who have picked up the slack while Edwards recovers from knee surgery.

The Wolves possess the No. 1-ranked defense in the NBA (104.0 rating), even getting LaMelo Ball to buy in and play the best defense of his career.

Ayo Dosunmu is averaging 21.0 points, 4.8 rebounds and 3.3 assists while shooting 46.7 percent in 11 starts filling in for Edwards. Terrence Shannon Jr. and Bones Hyland have stepped up as well.

When Edwards returns and if Ball stays healthy, this looks like one of the NBA's elite teams.

There's a lot of talent on this New Orleans Pelicans roster. The problem is, few of the pieces fit, some of them are hurt and one of them wants to be traded.

The Pelicans desperately need a trade (or two, or three) to better balance out this roster and actually try to make a playoff run. The defense is awful (118.4 rating, 27th overall ), there's precious little shooting (9.8 threes per game, 30th overall ) and ball movement is non-existent on some nights.

The positives? Zion Williamson has missed just one game and is at least occasionally shooting threes again. Saddiq Bey has been one of the NBA's best sixth men and Derik Queen looks deserving of a far bigger role.

Overall, an offseason of inactivity that looked like a mistake clearly was.

The defending champions have gone 8-3 since an 0-3 start to the season, with Jalen Brunson and Karl-Anthony Towns both posting All-Star caliber campaigns.

A sixth-ranked defense has been a pleasant surprise despite losing Mitchell Robinson in free agency to the Boston Celtics. Towns is leading the NBA in rebounding (14.1 per game), arguably having the best overall season of his career while he awaits a new contract.

Mikal Bridges and Josh Hart are only averaging a combined 14.0 points per game this season, with both shooting 28.9 percent or worse from outside the arc.

There's still a lot to be figured out for New York, although the last few weeks have been much better than the first.

Injuries have ravaged the Oklahoma City Thunder this season, a team that's still managed to stay in the playoff hunt in the West despite missing three starters.

Shai Gilgeous-Alexander (30.9 points per game, No. 2 overall in the NBA ) is doing his best to keep this offense afloat without Jalen Williams and Chet Holmgren, although OKC ranks just 17th overall this season.

Rookies Aday Mara and Bennett Stirtz have been thrown into the fire immediately while Ajay Mitchell is being asked to play a No. 2 scorer role for the first time in his career.

This team needs Holmgren to return as soon as possible while eyeing some mid-season trades. The championship window is still very much open.

A 4-1 record in their last five games has helped the Orlando Magic climb closer back to the .500 mark as the team awaits the return of Paolo Banchero from a high ankle sprain.

Franz Wagner has stepped up as a scorer and playmaker in his absence, averaging 24.2 points, 6.8 rebounds and a career-high 8.3 assists ( fifth-most in the NBA ). Desmond Bane and Anthony Black have helped carry the offensive load as well.

Normally a stout defensive squad, Orlando has fallen to 13th overall this season. This number will need to improve whether or not Banchero is on the floor, given the offensive flaws on this roster.

It would have been perfectly understandable to see the Philadelphia 76ers get off to a .500-ish start as they attempted to mesh LeBron James and Jaylen Brown alongside Tyrese Maxey and Joel Embiid. The fact that this group is in first place in the East with this good of a record already should be terrifying for the rest of the conference.

Philly's three losses have all been to good teams (Detroit Pistons, Cleveland Cavaliers, Boston Celtics), with the Sixers going a perfect 8-0 against squads with a losing record.

Maxey is wisely being prioritized as the No. 1 offensive option, although it's been the defense that's actually been the better ranked side of the ball for this group.

Health will continue to be monitored on a team with Embiid and James, but the early returns have been fantastic.

For a team that desperately needs a true point guard and is watching its starting lineup get destroyed on a nightly basis, the Phoenix Suns aren't in that bad of shape right now.

The core four of Devin Booker, Jalen Green, Dillon Brooks and Miles Bridges has a net rating of minus-23.7 in 410 total possessions this season (zero percentile, via Cleaning the Glass ). Still, all four have started all 13 games for the Suns.

This is the worst rebounding team in the entire NBA (46.6 total rebound percentage), one that's rotated starting centers while they await the return of Mark Williams from shoulder surgery.

Getting Williams back will help, but Green needs to be traded for a pass-first point guard. Players like Dejounte Murray, James Harden or Jrue Holiday would be strong veteran additions for Phoenix and help solve the floor general problem.

The Portland Trail Blazers rank 7th overall in offense, defense and net rating this season, good enough for a current playoff spot in the West.

Even a Ja Morant hamstring injury hasn't slowed Portland down, as Deni Avdija (24.2 points, 6.2 rebounds, 6.1 assists) is heading towards another All-Star season. Damian Lillard (20.1 points, 4.4 assists) looks great for a 36-year-old coming off a torn Achilles and Jrue Holiday could be headed for a Sixth Man of the Year award.

Is it officially time to call Scoot Henderson a bust? The fourth-year guard is struggling once again and averaged just 9.2 points and 1.0 assists on 21.1 percent shooting from three in his five starts.

It's been a predictably terrible season for the Sacramento Kings. Nine of the team's 12 losses have come by 10 points or more while the Kings rank 28th or worse on both sides of the ball.

Darius Acuff Jr. is an absolute stud, though. Say what you want about usage and shooting percentages right now, but the 20-year-old guard looks like a future 10-time All-Star with the ball in his hands. His averages of 25.5 points and 7.1 assists per game put him in extraordinary territory for a rookie.

Domantas Sabonis is second in the NBA in rebounding (13.2 per game) and should have some positive trade value to a contender who can use his all-around offensive game and glass-cleaning abilities.

For now, Kings fans should just enjoy the Acuff experience and not check the standings anytime soon.

A 12-game win streak was recently snapped, although the San Antonio Spurs should feel really good about their place in the standings right now.

There's clearly been no Finals hangover, as the Spurs' only losses have been to a full-strength Oklahoma City Thunder team on opening night as well as to the Houston Rockets and Detroit Pistons.

Victor Wembanyama (28.4 points, 12.0 rebounds, 3.3 assists, 1.1 steals, 4.1 blocks) could win MVP in addition to Defensive Player of the Year while Dylan Harper (18.4 points, 5.4 rebounds, 4.5 assists) is thriving as a starter.

Owners of the second-best net rating in all of basketball, the Spurs should be considered the championship favorites right now.

Even with an ugly record to begin the 2026-27 season, the Toronto Raptors still have a positive net rating and rank in the top half in both offense and defense overall.

Kawhi Leonard has been limited to just two games in his return to Toronto, leaving Scottie Barnes (23.8 points) and RJ Barrett (20.9 points) to carry the offensive load.

The Raptors need a better outside shooting attack, as they rank 25th overall in made threes (11.9 per game) and accuracy (33.3 percent).

Leonard would help fix much of what ails Toronto, meaning it's not time to panic just yet.

Injuries have ruined any chance at a playoff run for the Utah Jazz right now, as the members of the projected starting frontcourt—Lauri Markkanen, Jaren Jackson Jr. and Jusuf Nurkić—have played a total of 12 games this season between them. All three are currently sidelined due to injury.

No. 2 overall pick Darryn Peterson looks like a future All-Star and is averaging 16.9 points, 4.3 rebounds, 3.7 assists and 1.2 steals per game. Keyonte George is having another big year and Mo Bamba has been a pleasant surprise as a pickup off the scrap heap.

The Jazz had real playoff (or at least, play-in) hopes this year, especially since we've seen a young Memphis Grizzlies team make the leap to contender. This has been one of the most disappointing teams in the NBA, although injuries are mostly to blame.

Losers of eight of their past nine games, the Washington Wizards clearly aren't ready to be called contenders just yet.

Despite adding Trae Young's playmaking and Anthony Davis' rim protection, the Wizards rank 24th or worse on both sides of the ball this season. They've abandoned the development of some of their recent first-round picks in order to give veterans like Khris Middleton more minutes, which is absolutely the wrong thing to do.

Young's contract looks like the worst in the NBA right now. At least Washington didn't give Davis another max deal and could actually flip him at the deadline for a nice return if he continues his stellar play (24.5 points, 9.8 rebounds, 2.1 assists, 1.2 steals, 1.2 blocks).

articles.title: Jayson Tatum blames himself for Celtics' Nuggets loss after regretting critical moment that changed the game
articles.summary: Jayson Tatum took the blame for a technical foul that sealed the Boston Celtics’ 105-101 loss to the Denver Nuggets on Wednesday night.
articles.body: Jayson Tatum took the blame for a technical foul that sealed the Boston Celtics’ 105-101 loss to the Denver Nuggets on Wednesday night. Boston trailed by three with 6.4 seconds left after a Jamal Murray jumper and had a timeout to set up a game-tying try. Tatum then tossed the ball toward referee John Goble, and Eric Dalen, who stood closest, whistled him for a technical. Murray made the free throw to push the lead to four. Tatum said he was not angry, but he wished he had handed the ball to the official nearest him.Why did Jayson Tatum blame himself for the Celtics’ loss to the Nuggets?The Celtics star said the toss was never meant as a show of anger. He believed Goble was looking toward the Boston bench after the timeout, so he sent the ball that way. Dalen apparently saw it as attitude. Tatum pleaded his case to the official once more after the final buzzer, but the game was already gone.Still, Tatum owned the mistake. “I should have just probably gave the ball to the ref closest to me,” he said. He told Dalen he was not upset and did not think a foul was warranted, but he accepted a simple hand-off would have avoided the whole thing.Coach Joe Mazzulla said the team cannot hand officials a chance to read a play a certain way. “We just have to be better,” he said.The call capped a rough second half. Tatum scored 20 points before the break and four after it. He finished 10-for-23 from the floor, 3-for-9 from three, with three assists. He pointed to the four third-quarter turnovers as the moment Boston lost its rhythm.Foul gap and the road ahead for BostonBoston led 61-49 at halftime, then watched the night turn. The Celtics were called for 30 fouls to Denver’s 13, and the Nuggets shot 29 free throws to Boston’s 12. In the second half, the gap was 22-3. Paul George fouled out with more than six minutes left after just 22 minutes on the floor. Boston still had 48 points in the paint and 18 offensive rebounds.Denver’s defense did its part too. The Nuggets doubled Tatum and broke Boston’s flow in the third. After Neemias Queta’s hook shot with 7:55 left in the quarter, the Celtics turned it over on eight straight possessions. Tatum had four of them. Payton Pritchard and Mitchell Robinson were called for offensive fouls, and George sent a pass out of bounds. Mazzulla said Boston should welcome two defenders on the ball because it has passers who can make those reads. Queta called it a learning curve.The loss is Boston’s second straight and its first skid of the season. The Celtics are 11-4 and own one of the league’s best net ratings. They face the Kings in Sacramento next on a four-game road trip.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Luka Struggles in Loss to Jazz, Top Box Score Stats, Highlights for Peterson, Kessler, Top Players
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Lakers' nine-game winning streak came to an end Wednesday night as the Utah Jazz walked out of Crypto.com Arena with a 109-97 victory.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Lakers' nine-game winning streak came to an end Wednesday night as the Utah Jazz walked out of Crypto.com Arena with a 109-97 victory.

The Lakers' offensive output was their second-lowest of the season. The shots weren't falling for Los Angeles as it went 9-of-33 from beyond the arc.

The Jazz still own the second-worst record in the Western Conference (3-13), but the performances of Keyonte George, Ace Bailey and Darryn Peterson offered a lot of encouragement.

Bailey and George really stepped up in the fourth quarter, combining to score 19 points.

The Jazz defense did a great job on Lakers star Luka Dončić all night. He had 29 points but shot 10-of-28, including 2-of-12 from beyond the arc.

Along with scoring 31 points in the final frame to see through the win, Utah neutralized Dončić at the other end of the court in the fourth quarter. He had as many points as turnovers (three).

"Honestly, I just got to do way better than this," he told reporters after the game. "This is unacceptable for my part. I got to lead the team in better ways."

Dončić had some flashy dimes, but his nine turnovers were his second-most on the year. The Lakers were minus-18 with him on the floor.

Quentin Grimes had a few highlight-reel plays en route to a 20-point outing, while Walker Kessler posted his ninth double-double in his last 10 appearances.

The Lakers have a great opportunity to regroup as their next game comes against the 1-13 Sacramento Kings on Friday. Then they get a rematch against Utah to avenge Wednesday's defeat.

The Jazz face off with the Phoenix Suns on Friday and wrap up the week against the Dallas Mavericks, the first half of a back-to-back before their meeting with L.A.

articles.title: Lakers' Luka Doncic Takes Blame for 'Unacceptable' Performance vs. Jazz, 'Got to Do Way Better'
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Lakers' nine-game winning streak came to an end Wednesday night, and superstar guard Luka Dončić willingly shouldered the blame for the loss.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Lakers' nine-game winning streak came to an end Wednesday night, and superstar guard Luka Dončić willingly shouldered the blame for the loss.

Following L.A.'s 109-97 home loss at the hands of the Utah Jazz, Dončić told reporters, "Honestly, I just got to do way better than this. This is unacceptable for my part. I've gotta lead the team in better ways."

Dončić leads the NBA in scoring this season with 38.1 points per game, and although he finished with 29 points on Wednesday, he clearly wasn't at his best.

The 27-year-old veteran shot just 10-of-28 from the field and 2-of-12 from three-point range, plus he turned the ball over nine times in the loss.

It was a disappointing showing for Dončić and the Lakers as a whole considering one they pulled off one night earlier against the Charlotte Hornets.

Trailing by 13 points entering the fourth quarter, the Lakers stormed all the way back to force overtime and beat Charlotte 118-114 in the extra session. Quentin Grimes led the way with a career-high 47 points, while Dončić finished with 36.

Following Wednesday's loss, Lakers head coach JJ Redick suggested to reporters that the heavy workload Dončić has to carry may have impacted him, especially with Austin Reaves out due to injury and unable to shoulder some of the burden.

"I mean, the shot creation that is required from him, I think it takes its toll," Redick said. "That's the luxury of having two really elite creators, and obviously when they're both in the lineup, it makes things a little bit easier."

Dončić refused to make any excuses, though, telling reporters , "That can't be an excuse. All NBA teams play 82 games, so that can't be an excuse."

Wednesday did mark the end of a tough stretch for the Lakers, however, as they played back-to-back games and three games in four nights.

They will have Thursday off before welcoming in the Sacramento Kings on Friday, and after resting Saturday and Sunday, the 13-3 Lakers will get another crack at the 3-13 Jazz on Monday.

Many major events have happened between the releases of the Grand Theft Auto V and Grand Theft Auto VI video games, and the 2026-27 Washington Wizards snapping an eight-game winning streak can now be added to that list.

After the Wizards went on the road to beat the Toronto Raptors 103-99, giving them their first win since Nov. 2, rookie No. 1 overall draft pick AJ Dybantsa joked about the timing of the victory:

Washington prevailed shortly before GTA VI officially launched in North America at midnight ET on Thursday.

articles.title: Yaxel Lendeborg Hyped by Kyrie Irving in Video After Warriors-Mavs, 'Fell in Love With His Game'
articles.summary: Golden State Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg once described himself as "a big Kyrie guy," and the feeling is mutual.
articles.body:
Golden State Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg once described himself as "a big Kyrie guy," and the feeling is mutual.

Dallas Mavericks star Kyrie Irving heaped a lot of praise on Lendeborg after the two crossed paths in Dallas' 116-94 victory over Golden State on Wednesday. He told reporters after the game he "kind of fell in love" with Lendeborg's game after watching some of his college performances:

The nine-time All-Star went on to speak highly of Lendeborg's mentality. He believes the first-round pick is "a lot more honest" than the typical NBA player, and he has the awareness to understand what he needs to keep improving.

The Warriors have now dropped four games in a row, which coincides with star guard Stephen Curry's oblique injury. Curry's absence is putting a lot of pressure on Lendeborg, who's the team's second-leading scorer.

Against the Mavericks, he had 13 points on 6-of-18 shooting.

Golden State's short-term outlook was already pretty grim as it leaned on the aging core of Curry, Draymond Green and Jimmy Butler, who's still recovering from a torn ACL. Curry missing multiple weeks means losing valuable ground in the playoff race.

No matter how the rest of the year unfolds, Lendeborg looks like a player the franchise can build around in a post-Steph future. His peers across the league are taking notice too.

articles.title: How Damian Lillard has boosted Trail Blazers in promising return from Achilles injury
articles.summary: Even with Lillard not quite at the peak of his powers, his presence is being felt in Portland.
articles.body:
The fear, when we saw Damian Lillard sitting there with a thousand-yard stare after falling to the ground early in Game 4 of the Milwaukee Bucks' first-round series against the Indiana Pacers in the 2025 NBA playoffs, was that we might never see him again.

A ruptured Achilles tendon has altered, if not derailed, plenty of NBA careers. What would it do to a small guard with more than 35,000 NBA minutes on his odometer who was entering his mid-30s?

What if that — that false step, that unsatisfying whimper of a finish to his time in Milwaukee, an era that felt like an error almost from the moment it started — was the last time we'd ever see Lillard looking like what he'd been for the previous 13 years: among the most dangerous shooters of all time, a generational scoring threat from the second he crossed half-court, one of the 75 greatest players in the league's history ?

An awful lot's happened since then: the shocking waive-and-stretch that ended Lillard's time in Milwaukee (and, more or less, Giannis Antetokounmpo's time there); his subsequent re-signing with the Portland Trail Blazers, the home he never really seemed to want to leave; an entire season spent rehabilitating and recovering, in hopes of giving himself a shot at becoming himself once again.

"All the time off I had, I had to take advantage of it," Lillard recently told NBC . "Not just look at how far out I was and just try to chill or whatever. I had to make sure that every day counted. I was diligent in the process of my rehab, and then when I got back on the court, the weight room, making sure I was balanced on both legs. And then, once it got back to just hooping, that was the easy part — it was just a matter of shaking off the rust."

Fourteen games into his first action in 18 months, Lillard still hasn't totally shaken it all off and returned to the level that made him a nine-time All-Star and seven-time All-NBA selection. Entering Thursday's matchup against a Bucks team that now looks very different from the one for which he last played, he's averaging 20.1 points, 4.4 assists and 3.0 rebounds in 29.1 minutes per game, and shooting 39.6% from the field — all at or near career lows. He's driving to the basket less frequently than he has since 2013 ; just 15% of his field goal attempts are coming at the rim, far and away the lowest share of his career . Nearly 60% of his shots, conversely, are coming from 3-point land — by far the largest share of his life in the NBA.

He's had nights to forget in the early going, like scoring nine points on 3-for-13 shooting in a blowout loss to the Memphis Grizzlies, or finishing with nine on 2-for-15 shooting in Monday's loss to the Minnesota Timberwolves. Those two single-digit performances, by the way, are already as many as Dame has had in any whole season since 2014 .

Dame's also had moments to remember, though. Like dropping 25 points with a half-dozen 3-pointers in 24 minutes on the Phoenix Suns in Portland's season opener, his first live action in 543 days …

… or knocking down a side-step dagger in the right corner to hand the Los Angeles Lakers one of just three losses they've suffered on the season …

… or punctuating a 13-point third quarter against the Oklahoma City Thunder with a vintage, swashbuckling just-inside-the-logo buzzer-beating pull-up triple over the outstretched arms of 7-foot-3 rookie Aday Mara:

"I knew he was gonna shoot," Blazers two-way guard Chris Youngblood told Conor Bergin of Blazer's Edge after the win over OKC. "I was like, 'If this goes in, this crowd is about to go crazy.'"

Even amid the fits-and-starts with his finishing, Lillard has helped give Portland fans plenty to go crazy about in a pleasantly surprising start to the season — one in which he's been a lot more than just a nice story .

The Blazers enter Thursday at 9-5, in sixth place in the Western Conference, with the NBA's No. 8 offense and No. 10 defense, according to Cleaning the Glass . (The last time the Blazers ended a season in the top 10 on both ends of the floor: 2014-15 .) They've taken down Luka Dončić's Lakers in L.A. and Nikola Jokić's Nuggets in Denver, swept a two-game baseball series from Shai Gilgeous-Alexander's Thunder at Moda Center, and looked like a team capable of building on last season's return to the playoffs, ownership misadventures and personnel shuffling be damned.

Dame's done it in part by working his way into a new normal — one in which he's no longer the sun around whom the entire organization orbits, but rather one component of a constellation in which All-Star forward Deni Avdija often shines brightest.

Heading into the season, one of the main questions hanging over the Blazers was how first-year head coach Micah Nori would craft an offensive ecosystem that kept everything copacetic despite introducing two decorated All-Star on-ball playmakers (a returning Lillard, an incoming Ja Morant) alongside Avdija, who rose to prominence and helped return Portland to the postseason by becoming the league's highest-volume driver and establishing new career highs in usage, shot attempts, touches and time of possession. The early returns were positive: The Blazers are plus-19 in 66 minutes with Avdija, Lillard and Morant sharing the floor, scoring a scorching 125.9 points per 100 possessions in their minutes with both Dame and Ja taking a smaller slice of the total offensive pie .

The overarching experiment got paused when Morant went down with a hamstring strain , leading Nori to shuffle his starting lineup — first by sliding fourth-year guard Scoot Henderson into Morant's spot, and then, with Scoot struggling, swapping in 6-foot-6 forward Sidy Cissoko for a bigger, more defensively sound look. Portland's allowing just 106.5 points-per-100 with Cissoko on the court alongside ace defensive center Donovan Clingan and swingman Toumani Camara — a near-best-in-the-league level of point prevention.

Removing one ball-handler from the mix has somewhat reduced the need for offensive sacrifice, but Lillard has continued to keep up his end of the bargain. He is finishing 27.7% of Portland's offensive possessions with a shot attempt, foul drawn or turnover — his lowest usage rate since 2014-15, when he was setting up LaMarcus Aldridge. His on-ball percentage — literally the share of his floor time that he has the ball in his hands — is the second-lowest of his career.

Dame has never averaged fewer touches or a lower time of possession, spent less time operating in the pick-and-roll, or spent more time lurking as a catch-and-shoot option. Just under 19% of the offensive possessions Lillard has finished this season have come while spotting up away from the primary action, according to Synergy Sports Technology's tracking data — more than twice as much as in 2022-23, the final year of his first stint in the Pacific Northwest.

"Being on this team and having less responsibility than I had before, I don't have to make every play," Lillard told Sean Highkin of the Rose Garden Report . "I don't have to score every basket. I just came into this season mostly focused on how I could impact winning. I know that at the end of games, I'm gonna have to make shots and make plays and make free throws. But over the course of a game, I think the load is just lighter."

Deploying Lillard as a different sort of threat in a smaller-scale role has proven useful to the overall offensive operation for the Blazers, who are scoring like a top-five offense with Dame on the floor — and like a near-top- 10 unit when he's on the floor without Avdija , which were minutes in which Portland's offense died last season .

Last season, even with Avdija ascending as a downhill menace, primary playmaker and point-producing weapon, the Blazers finished the season just 20th in offensive efficiency , due partly to struggles with ball security (dead last in the NBA in offensive turnover rate , with 90 more live-ball turnovers than any other team in the league), shot-making (27th in team 3-point accuracy, 29th from midrange, 21st in overall effective field goal percentage) and half-court execution (just 29th in points per half-court possession ). The arrival of Lillard has helped: Portland has turned the ball over less frequently , generated a higher share of its shots from 3-point land , shot better in the midrange , and scored more efficiently in the half-court with Dame on the floor this season.

Even with Lillard not quite at the peak of his shot-making powers, his presence opens things up for the rest of the offense. With him on the floor, nearly 53% of Avdija's 2-point baskets have come via assist — 20 percentage points higher than when Dame sits . The driving lanes that were so often so congested last season are open a bit wider with defenses needing to account for Lillard, who ranks eighth in the NBA's gravity metric — a stat aiming to quantify "how much a player pulls defenders towards them [...] how much attention they draw compared to what the spacing on the floor predicts" — just south of one high-volume superstar scorer in a ball-handling timeshare (Donovan Mitchell) and two designated sharpshooters playing off high-usage primary creators (Klay Thompson, Duncan Robinson ).

That company feels illustrative of the space Lillard currently finds himself occupying: not peripheral, still vital, but more of a complement than a centerpiece. (He still can shift into primary mode, though; on Tuesday, with Avdija sidelined by a sore left foot, Dame scored a team-high 25 points with five assists against the Timberwolves, pushing the NBA's No. 1 defense to the brink in a game that Portland nearly, and perhaps should have, won .)

Plenty of superstars over the years have struggled to find comfort moving into that space. Perhaps due to the time away, though, Lillard seems to be navigating the shift fairly smoothly.

"Obviously, for the sake of rhythm and timing, you want to be on the ball sometimes, which I am," Lillard recently told Sam Amick of The Athletic . "But I think it just lessens the load of having to sometimes beat two guys, or get into the paint and do too much when we've got so many guys that can do that. I can space the floor, give guys space, and also catch and attack on the second side. It's been a process, kind of finding the spots, and it's becoming more natural. But it's been great as far as how I feel physically, how I'm able to play late in games, the effort and energy I'm able to give defensively throughout games. And I think it's a more sustainable way for us to handle the game."

Eighteen months ago, we wondered if we'd ever see Dame look like Dame again. While the jury's still out on that, what he's been so far — in terms of his combination of scoring and shooting efficiency , and by metrics like win shares per 48 minutes , box plus-minus , value over replacement player and player efficiency rating — nets out to something like a top-20 guard in the league. Just a month after coming back from one of the most devastating injuries an NBA player can suffer, that's not nothing … and, with a little more time, a little bit of luck and a lot more hard work, it's also not where Lillard's return is going to stop.

"This early in the season, I still feel like I'm getting it back completely — just that rhythm, and taking bumps, and moving at the pace of the league," Lillard told NBC . "But I'm feeling better and better. [...] I've just got to keep it rolling, and keep doing what I'm doing."

The Dallas Mavericks are off to a solid start (8-7) and have denied any desire to trading Kyrie Irving up until this point.

The sharks are circling nonetheless, and a surprising new team has reportedly emerged with preliminary interest, according to SNY's Ian Begley—the Utah Jazz:

articles.title: Julius Randle Rips Nets' 'Embarrassing' Loss to Bulls Amid Viral Video of Message to Team
articles.summary: It's taken less than a month of regular-season action for Brooklyn Nets veteran forward Julius Randle to reach his boiling point.
articles.body:
It's taken less than a month of regular-season action for Brooklyn Nets veteran forward Julius Randle to reach his boiling point.

Randle ripped his team for Wednesday night's 137-107 loss to the Chicago Bulls in front of a home crowd at the Barclays Center, which dropped the Nets' record to 3-11 this year.

"I don't know, that was embarrassing," Randle said after scoring 17 points in the loss. "Been in the league for 13 years and that's one of the worst games I've ever been a part of. It's not the score, it's the pride and effort."

The "pride and effort" of the Nets appears to be the true source of Randle's frustration, as he was seen yelling at his teammates during a timeout over their lack of fire:

To make matters worse, Wednesday's loss came while the Nets were celebrating "ABA Night" with Julius Erving, the greatest player in franchise history, in attendance.

"We didn't really talk to the players, the coaches doing all the talking and they were getting their preparation in, doing all their drills … I fully anticipated the Nets to be so fired up having us here, they would blow Chicago out. I'm looking at 62-39, so I was wrong," Erving said during the YES broadcast, per Brian Lewis of the New York Post .

Nets head coach Jordi Fernandez echoed Randle's criticisms of the team's effort.

"I can try to say it in Spanish, because in English they don't understand," Fernandez said. "So I'll keep trying and find whatever language works. But yeah, our effort was not good."

Randle, who was acquired from the Minnesota Timberwolves over the offseason, is one of the veteran leaders of a young Brooklyn squad, but it seems like even he's having trouble getting through to his teammates.

The Nets will try to end their three-game skid when they face the Orlando Magic (6-8) on Friday.

articles.title: 5-Star Ivanna Wilson Manyacka Commits to UCLA over UConn, Duke, Maryland, More Finalists
articles.summary: UCLA has kicked off its national title defense with a 4-0 start, and its outlook for 2027-28 is already looking bright.
articles.body:
UCLA has kicked off its national title defense with a 4-0 start, and its outlook for 2027-28 is already looking bright.

Five-star small forward Ivanna Wilson Manyacka confirmed to ESPN's Shane Laflin she committed to the Bruins. She's the No. 2 overall player in 247Sports' composite rankings for 2027.

Duke, LSU, Maryland and UConn were the other finalists who narrowly missed out.

New 2027 Men's NCAA Tournament Bracket Projections 🔮

247Sports' director of scouting Brandon Clay watched Wilson Manyacka compete in trials for the United States U17 team. He wrote she "may have the best high pick-up I've seen from a high school prospect, ripping the ball over a defender's head and finishing with a layup."

"The most dangerous part of Wilson-Manyacka's game is her versatility; she'll make a move like that high pick-up and then hit a 3-pointer on the next possession," Clay said.

Wilson Manyacka went on to represent Team USA in the FIBA U17 Women's Basketball World Cup and was named MVP for the tournament. She led the U.S. in scoring (12.9 points) while averaging 6.0 rebounds and 2.6 steals.

A lot of WNBA talent went out the door for the Bruins in the aftermath of their title. Six players, including stars Lauren Betts, Kiki Rice and Gabriela Jaquez, moved on to the pros.

As UCLA's schedule gets tougher, that talent drain could become a bigger problem for coach Cori Close.

Close is assembling a strong group for next year, though. In addition to Wilson Manyacka, the Bruins have commitments from Nation Williams, Finley Parcher and Anna Smykovskaia. Williams is 13th overall in 247Sports' composite rankings .

articles.title: New NBA Rumors on Trey Murphy III's Trade Status, Pelicans' Stance Amid Dejounte Murray Buzz
articles.summary: After veteran point guard Dejounte Murray requested a trade from the New Orleans Pelicans, teams are reportedly attempting to poach one of their other top young players.
articles.body:
After veteran point guard Dejounte Murray requested a trade from the New Orleans Pelicans, teams are reportedly attempting to poach one of their other top young players.

NBA insider Jake Fischer reported that the trade speculation surrounding Murray also "prompts various rival teams to resume their quests to pry Trey Murphy III away from New Orleans."

The swingman reportedly "is certainly aware of the widespread interest in his services," but he "has not formally pushed for relocation despite the Pelicans' long-term struggles." Fischer added that the team "remains reluctant to contemplate parting with the in-demand swingman."

HoopsHype's Michael A. Scotto added the Pelicans "could have gotten" at least two first-round picks for Murphy over the summer, though it's unclear where his value sits now.

Murphy has appeared in nine games this season and is averaging 15.6 points, 4.8 rebounds and 3.6 assists for a Pelicans team that ranks last in the Southwest Division with a 5-11 record. The 26-year-old has been sidelined with a knee injury, and he's had trouble staying on the court throughout his career, appearing in more than 70 games just once in his first five seasons in the NBA.

Still, Murphy is a talented 3-and-D wing who can contribute in a variety of ways when healthy. He's averaged at least three assists and one steal in each of the last three seasons. He has the type of two-way talent that teams covet, so it's not a surprise that the Pelicans aren't willing to let him go easily.

New Orleans is more motivated to get rid of Murray, who was sent home after his trade request became public. The disgruntled guard reportedly doesn't have many suitors, as his trade value has diminished around the league.

It's clear that the Pelicans will be major players in the trade market this season, but it remains to be seen if they will blow up their roster by trading Murphy and other young players in addition to their quest to ship Murray away.

articles.title: New NBA Trade Rumors on Dejounte Murray's Links to Heat, Suns Amid Landing Spot Buzz
articles.summary: The Phoenix Suns and Miami Heat are among the teams that have been linked to a possible move for New Orleans Pelicans' guard Dejounte Murray, though just how interested either team actually is remains up for debate.
articles.body:
The Phoenix Suns and Miami Heat are among the teams that have been linked to a possible move for New Orleans Pelicans' guard Dejounte Murray, though just how interested either team actually is remains up for debate.

According to NBA insider Jake Fischer , "it has been conveyed to me that the Suns would be asking for draft compensation to be added to the trade package for them to seriously consider a move for Murray. League sources say that Phoenix is definitely a franchise that Murray's camp sees as an attractive landing spot."

He added that "sources briefed on the Suns' thinking insisted to The Stein Line this week that the team does not regard point guard as its primary need."

Instead, the team sees center as a more important area to address, with Mark Williams injured and second-year man Khaman Maluach still a work in progress.

As for the Heat, Fischer reported that he's been "told that there has yet to be any meaningful contact between the Heat and Murray's camp."

The Suns got off to a rough start this season, going 3-6, and appeared as though they might need to consider shaking up the roster. They are 4-1 since, however, and have looked more like the team that made a surprise playoff appearance last season.

Adding a more natural point guard would make sense, taking pressure off Devin Booker to be both the leading scorer and main facilitator. And Jalen Green's $36.2 million salary would work straight up in a trade for a player like Murray ($32.7 million).

Still, guard isn't exactly a need for the team with Booker, Dillon Brooks, Green, Colin Gillespie, Jordan Goodwin and Luke Kennard currently on the roster and playing meaningful minutes. It's understandable why Murray might not be high on the team's list of potential moves.

The Heat would make more sense as a suitor, though the starting backcourt of Davion Mitchell and Klay Thompson has played well during the team's 9-6 start to the season. But it's fair to question if Mitchell can continue averaging career highs—by a wide margin—in both scoring (17.9 PPG) and assists (9.0 APG).

The 30-year-old Murray is having a down year (13.4 PPG, 4.4 APG) and has never quite been a hit in New Orleans. Any team trading for him is banking on him returning to the levels he once displayed with the San Antonio Spurs or Atlanta Hawks.

For the time being, however, it doesn't sound as though there is a major appetite around the NBA to take that gamble.

articles.title: New Kawhi Leonard Rumors on 'Mystery' Surrounding Knee Injury amid Raptors Absence
articles.summary: Toronto Raptors star Kawhi Leonard has missed the last 13 games while recovering from a knee injury, and questions continue to persist about the root cause of the issue.
articles.body:
Toronto Raptors star Kawhi Leonard has missed the last 13 games while recovering from a knee injury, and questions continue to persist about the root cause of the issue.

Michael Grange of SportsNet reported that "what is exactly wrong with Leonard and when he might return to the lineup remains a mystery."

Grange confirmed a report that described Leonard's injury as "patellar tendinopathy," also known as "Jumper's knee," which would require management throughout the season. However, multiple sources told Grange that it "is not the entire picture as it relates to his left knee," particularly because the swelling that initially caused him to be sidelined is not how that injury typically presents.

"And while no one I spoke with would say what precise condition Leonard was diagnosed with that explains the swelling, they did acknowledge it is another issue — not jumper's knee — that caused the problem and which has been the focus of the rest and treatment protocol over the past three-plus weeks," Grange wrote.

Still, sources told him that Leonard "is progressing well," and they "are confident that the mystery condition that has kept him out of the lineup to this stage won't be a season-long issue."

"We don't anticipate any setbacks after this," one source told Grange.

Leonard was expected to help lead the Raptors to title contention this season, but the team is currently 5-10 with a six-game losing streak.

Toronto will remain cautious with Leonard's return, but it's clear that the team needs him back in the lineup to avoid falling behind in the competitive Eastern Conference.

articles.title: Mark Walter reportedly nearing deal to sell LA Sparks to Padres owners for $750M
articles.summary: Walter has recently sold stakes in the Los Angeles Lakers and Chelsea of the Premier League.
articles.body:
José E. Feliciano and his wife, Kwanza Jones, are reportedly nearing a deal to purchase the Los Angeles Sparks for $750 million from Mark Walter, according to Sportico .

If the sale goes through, the $750 million price tag would break the WNBA record after the Connecticut Sun were bought by Houston Rockets owner Tilman Fertitta for $300 million in a plan to then move the franchise to Houston.

It was reported this week that Vanessa Bryant and Pau Gasol were interested in purchasing the Sparks, but Bryant posted on social media that she has not had any conversations about being a team owner.

"If that was true, I would announce it," Bryant wrote.

Walter has owned a majority stake in the Sparks since 2014, two years after his Guggenheim Partners consortium purchased the Los Angeles Dodgers. Like with the Dodgers, Walter has counted Magic Johnson, Todd Boehly, Robert Patton and Stan Kasten among his Sparks co-owners.

Walter has repeatedly said that he is not looking to sell his portfolio's biggest asset in the Dodgers.

News of this potential sale comes following considerable legal and financial scrutiny of Walter's non-sports businesses. Federal prosecutors have been looking into Walter's insurance firms since last fall , with questions about the number of deals they've made with companies also controlled by Walter, and whether those relationships were disclosed to the necessary people.

In August, MLB owners unanimously approved the then-MLB record $3.9 billion sale of the San Diego Padres to an ownership group led by Feliciano and Jones.

articles.title: Tyler Herro Reacts to Boos from Heat Fans After Trade to Bucks in Giannis Blockbuster
articles.summary: Milwaukee Bucks guard Tyler Herro says he wasn't surprised by the less than warm welcome he received from Miami Heat fans in his Wednesday return to Kaseya Center.
articles.body:
Milwaukee Bucks guard Tyler Herro says he wasn't surprised by the less than warm welcome he received from Miami Heat fans in his Wednesday return to Kaseya Center.

"It was fine. I'm on the other side now, so I expected it a little bit," Herro said Wednesday night, per the Miami Herald 's Anthony Chiang . "I'm on the other side, so things changed."

Herro was enthusiastically booed throughout the game, often as soon as he touched the ball, as he contributed eight points on 4-for-11 shooting in the Bucks' 137-130 loss.

Everything Giannis Said After Bucks Game

Herro was drafted by the Heat in 2019 and spent the first seven seasons of his career with the franchise.

The game marked the Bucks' first trip to Miami since the blockbuster trade that saw Herro and Giannis Antetokounmpo swap teams over the summer.

The Associated Press' Tim Reynolds reported shortly after the trade Herro had been involved in an "altercation" with former Heat teammate Bam Adebayo at NBA Summer League in Las Vegas over the summer.

Adebayo told reporters after the game he hadn't spoken to Herro and considered himself "on to the next thing."

Both Antetokounmpo and Adebayo topped 25 points in Wednesday's win, while Antetokounmpo came just short of a triple-double with 14 rebounds and nine assists to help the Heat improve to 9-6 after a slow start to the campaign. Herro and the Bucks fell to an NBA-worst 1-14 with the loss.
